message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two cards and loses a turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players sit in a circle. The first turn goes to the player left of the dealer. The direction of play can change with “Reverse” cards. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either:
• the color of the top discard card, **or**
• the number/symbol of the top discard card.
• A “Wild” card can be played on any card. | | **Special Cards** | | **Effect** | | **Draw Two** | Next player draws two cards and skips their turn. | | **Skip** | Next player loses their turn. | | **Reverse** | Reverses the direction of play (useful in 2‑player games: it becomes a “Skip”). | | **Wild** | You choose the new color. | | **Wild Draw Four** | You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. **(Must be played only if you have no other playable card; otherwise you can be challenged.)** | | **Challenging a Wild Draw Four** | If you suspect the player who played it had a playable card, you may challenge.
• If the challenger is correct, the player who played the Wild Draw Four must draw 4 cards.
• If the challenger is wrong, the challenger must draw 6 cards. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two cards as a penalty. | | **Ending a Round** | A round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by the other players:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Winning the Game** | First player to reach the target score (commonly 500) wins. You can also play a single round or set a different point goal. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep a “Wild” or “Draw Two” handy** – they’re great for ending a round or forcing opponents to draw. 2. **Watch the discard pile** – if you see a “Wild Draw Four” being played, consider challenging if you suspect the player had a playable card. 3. **Use “Reverse” strategically** – in a 2‑player game it acts like a “Skip,” giving you an extra turn. 4. **Plan your “UNO”** – if you’re about to finish, try to play a card that forces the next player to draw or skip, giving you a chance to finish the round. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
